title: Apply an explicitly configured zero relevance threshold
body:
## Problem

The shared recommendation preprocessing uses a truthiness check for min_rel_score. An explicitly configured zero threshold is skipped, so items with a zero rating are treated as irrelevant. This can also exclude users who should have relevant feedback and changes the resulting recommendation metrics.

## Change

Apply the threshold whenever min_rel_score is not None, including zero. Preserve the existing >= comparison, optional binary conversion, and no-feedback-user policy. Other threshold values and the unconfigured behavior remain unchanged.

## Validation

- 20 new cases on the upstream base: 8 failed, 12 passed.
- All recommendation metric tests with the fix: 58 passed on CPU.
- Direct preprocessing cases cover None, negative, zero and positive thresholds with both binary/graded data and both no-feedback policies; input frames are unchanged.
- Native current/reference Report cases check Precision, Recall, Hit Rate, MRR and NDCG against hand-calculated values for three users, with both scores and explicit ranks.
- Repository-pinned Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

This corrects the handling of an explicit zero threshold in the existing recommendation preprocessing. It does not change ranking, tie handling, metric formulas, or the meaning of a missing threshold. The full repository and notebook smoke suites were not run.
